sentences.text: The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus directing the respondent-Authority to pay compensation to the petitioner under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and restrain the respondents from carrying on any work on the fields of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
4. The case of the petitioner is that he is recorded tenure holder of Gata Nos. 850-ka, 816-ga, 469,
470, 471, 968 and 971, Village Fatehpur Sahaopur, Tehsil Chayal, District Kaushambi, along with other co-sharers.
The aforesaid land of the petitioner is situated near a road of Public Works Department (PWD).
It is alleged that PWD started widening of the road by 11 meters from the middle point.
It had acquired 4 meters land.
The project is part of Bouddh Circuit Road.
The petitioner and other villagers protested against the same and demanded compensation, which has not been paid to them so far.
This has compelled the petitioner to file the instant petition.

5. On 10.8.2023, the following order was passed: -
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.
2. In pursuance of previous order, Sub Divisional Magistrate has furnished instruction to learned Standing counsel, the same is taken on record.

According to it,
the land of petitioner is not affected by the project.
The instructions furnished by the respondent is not supported by any evidence.
3. Let an inspection of the site be made by revenue team comprising of three persons.
They will clearly demarcate the land of the petitioner on the site plan and mention the area, which is now in his possession and will also trace the road on the map.
The demarcation will be carried out in presence of the petitioner.

The District Magistrate,
Kaushambi after due verification of the facts stated in the report will submit the same before this Court along with his affidavit.

4. The District Magistrate will be personally liable in case the report is found to be incorrect or against the site position.
5.
List as fresh on 24th August, 2023.
6. Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing counsel will communicate the instant order to respondent no.2 for proper compliance.
6. In compliance of the above order, District Magistrate, Kaushambi has filed his personal affidavit.

The stand taken in paragraph nos. 9 and 10 of the said affidavit is as follows: -
9. That it is respectfully submitted that according to site plan Sheetaal S/o Kalidin,
Lallu Singh (petitioner), Ram Singh, Amar Singh all sons of Sahdev, Smt. Aasha Devi Wife of Moti Lal, Dharam Narayan Son of Bhagirathi, Sandip Kumar, Pradip Kumar S/o Bhan Singh and Aasha Devi W/o Bhan Singh are owner of plot no. 968 area Lallu Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169626074/
2 0.1250 hect (according to Khatauni) Plot no.971 0.0098 plot no. 530 K. area 0.0092 hect total 0.1440 are recorded in accordance with Khatauni but the petitioner and other co-sharers are in possession of land area 0.1746 which is excess to the Khatauni, Plot no.530-Kha area recorded as Banjar, Lallu Singh (petitioner) Ram Singh, Amar Singh Sons of Sahdev are owner of Plot No. 469, 470, 471, 472, 473, 474 which are connected to each other.

entities.text: Lallu Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Total area of aforesaid Plot no. 0.4793 as per Khatauni.
The petitioner Lallu Singh, Ram Singh and Amar Singh are in actual possession over the land area 0.5211 hect, which is more than area recorded in Khatauni.

10. That it is further submitted that land of the petitioner has not been encroached and used by the respondents authorities till now, but in future if the land of the petitioner is acquired, it will be acquired in accordance with the law.

7. Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel, submits that upon actual demarcation, it transpired that in fact the petitioner is in possession of excess area than what is owned by him and the other co-sharers.

8. Having regard to the above stand of the State respondents, we are not inclined to enter into questions of fact and decide the issue as to whether the respondents have encroached over the land of the petitioner or it is the petitioner who is in possession of some part of the chak road.
We leave it open to the petitioner to avail such other remedy as may be advised.
In that event, no observation made in the instant order will influence the proceedings.
9. The petition stands disposed of with the above liberty reserved in favour of the petitioner.

(Donadi Ramesh, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 13.9.2023 Jaideep/-
